title: Couscous Royale
subtitle: North African celebration couscous with mixed meats and vegetables
excerpt: Couscous royale is the grand version of North African couscous -- a generous spread of spiced broth with chicken, lamb, and merguez sausages piled over steamed couscous with slow-cooked vegetables. It is a celebration dish that takes time but feeds a crowd.
sourceNotes: Couscous has been eaten across North Africa for over a thousand years. Royale refers to the abundance of proteins -- traditionally three meats. It is the version served at Algerian and Moroccan weddings and family celebrations, and became well-known in France through the North African diaspora.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The broth and meats can be made 1 day ahead. Reheat gently and prepare the couscous fresh.

content.text: Merguez sausages are the ideal choice here -- if you cannot find them, any spiced lamb or beef sausage works. The couscous is steamed rather than boiled for a lighter, fluffier texture. Cover the bowl tightly after adding the stock and leave it for exactly 5 minutes.

items.prepNote: use 300g couscous -- place in bowl, cover with 350ml boiling stock, cover and steam 5 minutes

content.text: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over high heat. Brown the chicken and lamb pieces in batches. Remove and set aside.
Add the cinnamon and cumin to the pot. Stir for 30 seconds. Pour in the stock. Return the chicken and lamb.
Add the carrots and salt. Bring to the boil, then reduce to a simmer. Cover and cook for 30 minutes.
Add the courgettes and chickpeas. Cook for another 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, fry or grill the sausages in a separate pan until cooked through and browned. Set aside.
Place the couscous in a large bowl. Pour over 350ml of boiling stock or water. Cover tightly and leave for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork. Stir in a knob of butter if you like.
Pile the couscous onto a large platter. Arrange the meats and vegetables on top. Serve the broth in a bowl on the side for people to ladle over.

items.cause: Not enough water or not fluffed while still hot
items.fix: Use the correct ratio of 300g couscous to 350ml boiling liquid; fluff immediately with a fork when you lift the cover
Lamb neck should braise for at least 50 minutes total; check by pressing -- it should yield easily
Remove the meats and vegetables and simmer the broth uncovered for 10 minutes to concentrate it

content.text: Couscous royale is as much a Parisian dish as it is a North African one. It arrived in France with Algerian and Moroccan immigrants and has been served in North African restaurants across Paris since the 1950s. In Morocco and Algeria, couscous is traditionally eaten on Fridays after the midday prayer, using whatever meats the household has available.
